claims: `terraform test` fails — the HCL test wasn't updated with the template: `alerts/rules/peg-rule-definitions.tftest.hcl:68-69` still asserts the Slack title template contains `$alert.Annotations.summary` and `$alert.Annotations.resolved_summary`, but the new emoji-only title (`alerts/rules/peg-message-templates.tf:13-16`) has neither

A breach that starts out of an `Error` state loses its raise event and reports the wrong magnitude — `peg-alert-events.ts:109-110` and `:320-321`: `Error → Alerting` is now classified `error-recovered-alerting` and keyed into the `:error` cycle, so it no longer opens the `:alert` cycle

The later `Alerting → Normal` then finds no open raise and falls through to the `unpairedCleared` fallback at `:346` — the path meant for raises that happened before the query window — which uses the resolving line as evidence (`:262`), so the alert history reports the breach as 12 bps and drops both the onset entry and the duration (a regression vs base)
The branch's own test only covers `Alerting → Error → Alerting`, where an alert cycle is already open, which is why it passes (finding 2 is behavioral and not covered by any existing test)

The new `Error` query is a single point of failure for the whole panel — `ui-dashboard/src/app/api/peg-monitoring/alerts/route.ts:63-83`: `fetchJson` now issues a second request and `Promise.all`s it, so a failure on the supplementary `current=Error` / `previous=Error` query rejects and `GET`'s catch returns 502, blanking Recent Alerts even when the primary Alerting/Normal history came back fine
Upstream request count per poll goes 2 → 4, each with its own 8s timeout and 4 MB cap

Minor: the new lint slice is declaration-order dependent — `scripts/alerts/alert-rules-lint.test.mjs:1215-1220`: `slackTitleTemplate` is a `slice` between two `indexOf` results, so if the two resources are ever reordered in `peg-message-templates.tf`, start > end yields `""` and both `!slackTitleTemplate.includes(...)` assertions pass vacuously

1.why: peg-rule-definitions.tftest.hcl:68-69 does still assert the emoji-only peg_slack_title contains $alert.Annotations.summary/resolved_summary, but this is the known 'Update the stale Terraform title assertion' item at peg-message-templates.tf:14

2.why: peg-alert-events.ts:109-110 maps Error→Alerting to error-recovered-alerting, and :318-321 make it a non-opening transition keyed to `identity:error`, so unlike base (where current==='Alerting' was always 'raised') a breach starting from Error never opens the :alert cycle

3.why: the later Alerting→Normal keys to `identity:alert`, finds no open raise and no observedRaised, so :346 stores it in unpairedCleared and :354-355 phrase it with no raise — evidence falls back to the resolving line (:262) and the `lasted …` detail (:270) plus the onset event are dropped

4.why: coverage commentary on claim 2 with a false premise — the new 'Alerting to Error to Alerting' test (route.test.ts) opens only an :error cycle (Alerting→Error is classified 'error'), no alert cycle; it names no defect of its own

5.why: route.ts:63-83 does Promise.all a second Error-state request and GET's catch returns 502, but the route already fails closed on any upstream failure by design (base's two queries were equally fatal); a robustness preference, not a malfunction

6.why: factually true (4 fetches per poll, each with AbortSignal.timeout(8_000) at :74 and the 4 MB cap at :21/:80) but states no concrete defect

7.why: alert-rules-lint.test.mjs:1215-1220 does slice between the two indexOf results, but peg_slack_title precedes peg_slack_message in peg-message-templates.tf so the slice is non-empty today; a hypothetical-reorder fragility note, no current defect
